topic: How do on-board storage constraints influence payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged service prioritization?
response: On-board storage constraints limit the size of data packets that can be stored for time-tagged services (ðj tt d j þ). This directly influences the power allocation for these services, as they require more data storage, potentially increasing the need for larger power-hungry payloads. Immediate services, on the other hand, don't require on-board storage, allowing for more efficient power allocation.
